stops.name: St Mark's Basilica
stops.en: Visit the famous bronze horses.

stops.name: Doge's Palace
stops.en: Don't miss the guided tour named Secret Itinerary, which will let you discover the part of the palace where the city's administration worked, as well as Casanova's jail and the wonderful five hundred year old roof structure. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Santa Maria della Salute
stops.local: Basilica di Santa Maria della Salute
stops.en: As a votive offering for the city's deliverance from the Black Plague, the church was designed in the then fashionable Baroque style. Construction began in 1631. Most of the objects of art housed in the church bear references to the Black Death. Because of its location between the Grand Canal and the Giudecca Canal, its dome was an important addition to the Venice skyline and soon became emblemati

stops.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
stops.en: Venice's most significant art museum which is also one of Italy's best. Among the most important paintings in the Accademia are: Gentile Bellini: Procession on St. Mark’s Square (1496) and Miracle of the Cross at the Bridge of S. Lorenzo (1500), Giovanni Bellini: Pieta (1500), Jacopo Bellini: Madonna with Child and Cherubs (ca. 1450), Paris Bordenone: A fisherman presents the ring of St. Mark to t

stops.name: Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana
stops.en: Buildings by Sansovino, most important collection of books in Venice.

stops.name: Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
stops.local: Basilica di Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
stops.en: The big friary church, fine example of Venetian Gothic architecture, with fine monuments and paintings of Titian, Belliniand Donatello, among which the famous 'Assunta' by Titian.

stops.name: Church of San Giorgio Maggiore
stops.en: Designed by Andrea Palladio and build 1566-1610. Very nice views of Venice from the bell tower.

stops.name: Santi Giovanni e Paolo
stops.local: Basilica dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo (Venezia)
stops.en: A fine, huge Dominican church with the tombs of many Doges. It shares its piazza with the fine Renaissance façade of the Scuola San Marco and an equestrian statue of the mercenary captain Bartolomeo Colleoni (see below).

stops.name: Ca' Pesaro
stops.en: Beautiful palace housing the gallery of modern art focusing on Italian art in the 19th century as well as the Marco Polo Museum, a rich collection mainly of Asian exhibits (fabrics, clothes, armours, porcelain). A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Bridge of Sighs
stops.en: Connecting the Doge's Palace with the prison. Persons convicted in the palace were passing to prison here, seeing the last of Venice before going into the dark prison area with no daylight. You can pass the bridge yourself during a visit to the Doge's Palace or view it from outside from the Ponte della Paglia.

stops.name: St Mark's Campanile
stops.en: The current tower dates from 1912; an exact replica of the previous tower which collapsed in 1902. The top of the tower offers great views of Venice and the lagoon.

stops.name: Venetian Ghetto
stops.en: While racial and ethnic neighborhoods had existed prior to the Venetian Ghetto, Venice's ghetto was the first "ghetto" (coming from a Venetian word for the Iron Foundry that had been on the site) and "ghetto" eventually came to mean any neighborhood that was made up of a single ethnic/racial group. Today, Jewish life is still very active in the ghetto, and elsewhere in Venice, and is home to five

stops.name: Palazzo Grassi
stops.en: Contemporary art museum. Temporary exhibitions from François Pinault's Collection.

stops.name: Santa Maria dei Miracoli, Venice
stops.local: Chiesa di Santa Maria dei Miracoli (Venezia)
stops.en: A perfect jewel box church, simple in form but ornamented with fine exterior marble facings.

stops.name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
stops.en: Offers a personal collection of modern art collected by Peggy Guggenheim. Peggy was an American married to modern artist Max Ernst, and funded a number of his contemporaries. The gallery includes a sculpture garden and works by Picasso, Kandinsky, Gorky, Tanguy, Duchamp, Pollock, Dali, and Mondrian.

stops.name: St Mark's Clocktower
stops.en: Having been closed for restoration for many years, the restored astronomical clock is now visible. The fascinating tour of the clock mechanism (and rooftop bell) can only be visited on a guided tour, in English: M-W at 10:00 and 11:00, on other days at 14:00 and 15:00, in French M-W at 14:00 and 15:00, advance reservation required online or by phone at +39 041 5209070. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Museo Correr
stops.en: Interesting collection of globes, starting from the 16th century. There is also an only library hall, an archeological museum of Roman antiques and an important picture gallery. The museum offers a tour of Venetian history. Remarkable painting gallery with masterpieces of the 14th to 16th centuries from Venice, works of the Venetian sculpture Canova, studies on urban development and social life. A

stops.name: San Pietro di Castello
stops.local: Basilica di San Pietro di Castello
stops.en: Venice cathedral up to 1807, when the see was transferred to San Marco.

stops.name: Torcello Cathedral
stops.en: Precious mosaics, dating from Byzantine times, in the oldest cathedral in the lagoon of Venice. Campanile closed for restoration.

stops.name: Museo Archeologico Nazionale, Venice
stops.en: Collection of ancient Greek and Roman sculptures, Egyptian, Assyrian and Babylonian artefacts.

stops.name: State Archives of Venice
stops.en: One of the largest archives in the world, in an old Franciscan monastery. Manuscripts, texts and documents related to the history of the Venetian Serenissima.

stops.name: Museo provinciale di Torcello
stops.en: Collection of Greek and Roman finds, archaeological finds from the estuary from Paleo-Veneto and Etruscan periods.

stops.name: Galleria Internazionale d'Arte Moderna
stops.en: Modern art collection, paintings of the 19th and 20th century. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Rialto Bridge
stops.en: The bridge has become one of Venice's most recognizable icons and has a history that spans over 800 years. Today's Rialto Bridge was completed in 1591 and was used to replace a wooden bridge that collapsed in 1524.

stops.name: Madonna dell'Orto
stops.en: With the grave and 10 paintings of Jacopo Robusti (Tintoretto) (1578-1594), and his tomb.

stops.name: San Francesco della Vigna
stops.local: Chiesa di San Francesco della Vigna

stops.name: San Giacomo di Rialto
stops.local: Chiesa di San Giacomo di Rialto
stops.en: This church is possibly the oldest church in Venice built around 421. It is most recognized for its 15th-century clock above the entrance of the church. It is also recognized for the red pillars and beautiful gold accents around the church itself.

stops.name: San Salvador
stops.en: Includes the tomb of Caterina Cornaro, Queen of Cyprus (1454-1510).

stops.name: Santa Maria degli Scalzi
stops.local: Chiesa di Santa Maria di Nazareth (Venezia)
stops.en: Also known as Church of the Scalzi (Chiesa degli Scalzi), being the seat in the city of the Discalced Carmelites religious order (scalzi in Italian means "barefoot"). Built in the mid 17th century to the designs of Baldassarre Longhena and completed in the last decades of that century.

stops.name: Statue of Bartolomeo Colleoni
stops.en: The famous condottiere (1395–1475) had a long and remunerative career as captain of a mercenary army fighting for (or against, depending on the pay) the Republic, but died without an heir (8 daughters did not count) and bequeathed most of his significant wealth to Venice - on the condition that the grateful populace erect a monument to him in front of San Marco. The crafty council fulfilled the co

stops.name: Punta della Dogana
stops.en: Former customs house, centre for contemporary art, permanent exhibition of works from the François Pinault Collection. Renovation by world renowned architect Tadao Ando.

stops.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
stops.en: A masterpiece of Tintoretto, this guild house is an exquisite example of Mannerist art at its best. In order to allow a comfortable admiration of the detailed ceiling, mirrors are offered to the visitors. Cycles of allegories, life and passion of Christ, scenes from the Old and New Testament.

stops.name: Santo Stefano, Venice
stops.local: Chiesa di Santo Stefano (Venezia, San Marco)

stops.name: Gesuati
stops.en: 18th-century Dominican church on the Giudecca canal. The classical style building has a well-lit interior and is exceptional in preserving its original layout and Rococo decoration intact. The church and almost all its sculpture and paintings were created within a 30-year period: construction began in 1725, the church was consecrated in 1743, and the last sculptural decoration was in place by 1755

stops.name: Santa Maria Formosa
stops.en: The first church dedicated to "Mary of the Forms" was built on this spot in the VII century, when the Virgin ordered bishop Magnus to erect one, appearing to him as an exceedingly shapely woman. The current building, planned by Codussi, dates from the early XV century.

stops.name: Santa Maria della Pietà
stops.en: A church that used to house an orphanage and hospital in the 18th century, it is known among classical music enthusiasts as the church where the Catholic priest and composer Antonio Vivaldi worked for most of his career.

stops.name: San Giovanni in Bragora
stops.local: Chiesa di San Giovanni in Bragora

stops.name: San Sebastiano
stops.en: 16th-century Roman Catholic church, houses a cycle of paintings by the artist Paolo Veronese as well as paintings by Tintoretto and Titian. Includes the tomb of Paolo Veronese, a painter from Verona whose career was in Venice (1528-1588).

stops.name: San Nicolò dei Mendicoli
stops.local: Chiesa di San Nicolò dei Mendicoli

stops.name: campo San Polo
stops.en: A large campo (square), one of the most popular Carnival venues and also used for open-air concerts and screenings during the Venice Film Festival.

stops.name: I Gesuiti
stops.en: Also known as Church of Santa Maria Assunta, the current structure dates back to 1729.

stops.name: San Michele in Isola
stops.local: Chiesa di San Michele in Isola

stops.name: San Giacomo dell'Orio
stops.local: Chiesa di San Giacomo da l'Orio
stops.en: Founded in the 9th century, the current church was built in 1225.

stops.name: Tolentini
stops.local: Chiesa di San Nicola da Tolentino (Venezia)
stops.en: Historic church completed in 1714.

stops.name: San Simeone Piccolo
stops.en: The last church built in Venice. One of the things that it is recognized for is the fact that they celebrate Tridentine Mass on Sundays. It is also recognized for its dome because it is used to make the church look taller than it is and the dome itself is entirely covered with lead sheet.

stops.name: Santa Maria dei Carmini
stops.local: Chiesa di Santa Maria dei Carmini
stops.en: Large 14th-century Roman Catholic church.

stops.name: Scuola di San Giorgio degli Schiavoni
stops.en: Famous painting cycle by Vittore Carpaccio depicting the lives of St.George, Tryphon and Jerome.

stops.name: San Nicolò al Lido
stops.en: Monastery and church that houses some relics of Saint Nicholas (270–343 AD), patron of sailors. Both the church and monastery dates back to the 16th century.

stops.name: Giardini della Biennale
stops.en: They are the largest green area in the historic center and are home to the Venice International Art Exhibition. The gardens contain lush vegetation, among which the various twentieth-century architectures of the pavilions are organised, mostly around a central avenue from which smaller paths branch off, characteristic for their shape and each one bearing the name of the nation hosted.

stops.name: Scuola Grande dei Carmini
stops.en: Painting cycles dedicated to the Madonna del Carmine, canvases by Tiepolo and Padoviano.

stops.name: Scuola Grande di San Giovanni Evangelista
stops.en: Monumental staircase by Codussi, splendid San Giovanni Salon, Oratory of the Cross with precious reliquiaries.

stops.name: Palazzo Loredan Cini
stops.en: Former residence of Italian industrialist Vittorio Cini who amassed large collection of Italian art. The gallery houses a collection of 15th and 16th cent paintings from Tuscany and Ferrara, period furniture, silver, ivory and ceramic objects.

stops.name: Casa di Goldoni
stops.en: Birthplace of Venice's most famous playwright. Museum, library and theater studies center. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Giorgio Cini Foundation
stops.en: Multi-functional centre in an old Benedictine dormitory, the heart of the Foundation's library complex

stops.name: Giardini Papadopoli
stops.en: One of the few public parks in Venice.

stops.name: Palazzo da Mula
stops.en: The summer residence of the Venetian patricians. The façade features large Gothic windows and Veneto-Byzantine patere and panels from the 12th and 13th centuries. It is one of the few palazzi which escaped the restructuring of the island in the 1800s.

stops.name: Museo Ebraico di Venezia
stops.en: Objects related to the social life of the Jewish community, in two synagogues of the 16th century.

stops.name: Cemetery of San Michele
stops.en: Cemetery established following Napoleon Bonaparte's edict of 1804, part of the European circuit of monumental cemeteries. The Russian ballet director Sergei Diaghilev, the Austrian physicist Christan Doppler, the American poet Ezra Pound, the Russian composer Igor Stravinsky and the German-Italian composer Ermanno Wolf-Ferrari are buried in San Michele Cemetery.

stops.name: Museo diocesano d'arte sacra Sant'Apollonia
stops.en: Religious furniture and objects from now demolished churches and convents, one of the most appealing Romanesque cloisters of Venice.

stops.name: Santa Fosca
stops.en: Has the form of a Greek cross, which is surrounded by a semi-octagonal porticus.

stops.name: Museo Fortuny
stops.en: Collection of paintings and lamps. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: votive temple of Santa Maria Immacolata
stops.en: Military memorial dedicated to Italian soldiers of World War I and II.

stops.name: Scuola dell'Angelo Custode
stops.en: The only Lutheran church in Venice.

stops.name: Galleria Giorgio Franchetti Ca' d'Oro
stops.en: A collection of paintings and statues in a former palace from the 15th century. One of the best examples of Gothic architecture in Venice, sculptures, bronzes, paintings of Mantegna, Giorgione and Titian, Flemish and Dutch paintings.

stops.name: Oratorio dei Crociferi
stops.en: Small oratory facing the old monastery dei Crociferi, painting circle by Palma the Younger.

stops.name: Museo Storico Navale
stops.en: Collection of relics from the Serenissima Republic of Venice, the Italian navy, and the ancient Arsenale shipyards, miniature models, uniforms and stadarts, collection of sea shells. The main building of the Naval Historical Museum (Riva S. Biasio) is closed for renovation works. It's possible to visit the Ships Pavilion in rio della Tana, Castello 2162 (close to the Naval Museum).

stops.name: Fondazione Querini Stampalia
stops.en: Residence-museum of the Querini-Stampa family, library, picture gallery, furniture and household objects from the 16th cent onwards, important paintings by Bellini, Palma, Ricci, Tiepolo and Longhi.

stops.name: Byzantine Pictures Museum (Greek Institute)
stops.en: Collection of Greek, Cretan and Venetian icons of the 14th to 18th century.

stops.name: Palazzo Grimani
stops.en: A jewel of Renaissance architecture that was opened as a Venetia civic museum in 2008, collections of paintings, archaeological collection of Greek and Roman artefacts, temporary exhibitions.

stops.name: ASAC Library
stops.en: An annex at the Biennale gardens where the Biennale keeps records related to the Biennale exhibitions and to 20th century art, from 1895 onwards.

stops.name: Monuement for Gentile Bellini
stops.en: Venetian painter and official portraitist of the Doges (1439-1507), tomb.

stops.name: Monument for Giovanni Caboto
stops.en: Venetian explorer of North America who worked for the British (c. 1450-c. 1500).

stops.name: Giuseppe Verdi
stops.en: Composer of operas; Italian nationalist and national hero (1813-1901).

stops.name: Richard Wagner
stops.en: German opera composer (1813-1883).

stops.name: Ca' Rezzonico - Museum of 18th Century Venice
stops.en: Museum of the 18th century in Venice - attempts to revive the domestic atmosphere of Venetian nobilities. Furniture, interior decoration, paintings by Guardi, Canaletto, Tiepolo. On the third floor important paintings of the Venetian school. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Le Macchine di Leonardo a Venezia
stops.en: An exhibition in the Chiesa di San Barnaba showing around forty models of machines reproduced from Leonardo's codices. Some of the exhibits are interactive and copies of the codices are available for further reading. The church is an attraction in itself: it's the one under which Indiana Jones finds catacombs in The Last Crusade, by the way).

stops.name: Leonardo da Vinci Museum Venice
stops.en: Small museum dedicated to the life and work of Leonardo da Vinci.

stops.name: Funerary monument of Claudio Monteverdi
stops.en: Tomb, composer (1567-1643) and champion of the early Baroque seconda pratica and then-new genre of opera.

stops.name: Natural History Museum
stops.en: 11 exhibition halls with sections on palaeontology, explorations and nature. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Mocenigo Palace Museum
stops.en: A collection of clothes dating from the 18th century. Splendid interior. Collection of dresses and accessories, fabrics, books, figurines in various period costumes. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Telecom Italia Future Centre
stops.en: Centre dedicated to telecommunication technology. The building complex includes an adjacent church with important works of art, the Refectory (which is a conference hall today), Renaissance cloisters and a small museum focusing on the evolution of the telephone in the last 100 years.

stops.name: Scala Contarini del Bovolo
stops.en: A cylindrical tower with a spiralling series of arches, among the most characteristic examples of Venetian architecture at the period of transition from Gothic to Renaissance styles. From the top there are great panoramic views of the city.

stops.name: Music Museum
stops.en: Beautiful church, collection of musical instruments, Venetian Baroque paintings. Interpreti Veneziani, the creators of the Music Museum, also offer concerts in the nearby San Vidal church.

stops.name: Lace Museum
stops.en: There is a small lace museum called Museo del Merletto. Opinions on it vary from "not much to see" to "I didn't think I was interested in lace, but I spent 90 minutes in there". A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Basilica dei Santa Maria e San Donato
stops.en: Known for its twelfth-century Byzantine mosaic pavement, which is a similar floor to Venice's Basilica di San Marco, and the mosaic dome in the apse of the Virgin Mary. It is said to house the bones of the dragon slain by Saint Donatus. The bell tower, like most bell towers, is separate from the Church.

stops.name: Chiesa di San Pietro Martire
stops.en: Built in the 15th century and then reconstructed some years later after a fire. Inside are some art works, such as two canvasses by Bellini.

stops.name: Glass Museum
stops.en: Housed in the large Palazzo Giustinian near the island's center. "Museo Vetrario" in Italian, offers a century-by-century tour of Venetian glass-making. Roman glass pieces dating to the 1st to 3rd cent AD. Largest collection of historical glass with pieces dating from the 15th to 20th centuries. A MUVE museum.

stops.name: Old Jewish Cemetery - Lido
stops.en: Over thousand tombstones dating from 1550 to early 18th century. Guided tours on Sat from May to Oct (Italian and English), booking required.

stops.name: Venice Lido Planetarium
stops.en: Optical-mechanical structure, realistic reproduction of the celestial globe.

stops.name: Mekhitarist Monastery
stops.en: Library with historical manuscripts, collection of works, miniatures and documents of the Armenian history, Monastery Church. Tours in Italian, English, and Armenian. On the small island of San Lazzaro degli Armeni.

eats.name: E Rosa Salva
eats.note: One of the favorites is the mini-chain "E Rosa Salva", with three locations in the center - on C. Fiubera (from Piazza San Marco, take the underpass in the middle of the arcade, cross the bridge and t

eats.name: Crepes House by PePe
eats.note: Savory and sweet crepes

eats.name: Al Timon
eats.note: Warm and local atmosphere in this little osteria where they serve great Italian vintages by the glass. If you're adventurous, try their tasty tripe. Good music inside, some table by the canal in the s

eats.name: La Colombina
eats.note: Artfully presented Venetian cuisine

eats.name: Trattoria Alla Fontana
eats.note: Warm canalside restaurant

eats.name: Ristorante Casa Bonita
eats.note: Generous portions of pasta and seafood

eats.name: Vino Vero
eats.note: Small wine bar with excellent selection, away from the tourist crowds. Outdoor seating next to one of the canals.

eats.name: Al Parlamento
eats.note: Another small bar, away from the main tourist arteries. Serves spritz, cocktails and beer with a view of the Cannaregio canal.

eats.name: Cip ciap
eats.note: Also sells delicious takeaway pizza by the slice (or slab) at similar prices. They also serve very tasty mini pizzas per kilogram.

eats.name: Osteria Alla Rampa
eats.note: A bistro

eats.name: Al Vecio Canton
eats.note: This small and atmospheric restaurant/pizzeria will absolutely enchant you. Famous for its traditional style pizza and seafood pasta, you will not only get it all at affordable prices (pizza from €7.5

eats.name: Al Giardinetto
eats.note: Just behind the Piazza San Marco, this restaurant has a large private courtyard welcoming guests during good season. Seafood courses and Venetian specialities are served by Severino family.

eats.name: Pub Taverna L'Olandese Volante
eats.note: Located between the Rialto Bridge and Piazza San Marco. During the summertime there are tables outside when you can easily sit and rest after a day of wandering around this marvelous city. What is mor

eats.name: Pizza al volo
eats.note: Sells superb pizza by the (extremely large) slice in Campo Santa Margherita for approximately €1.80 a slice, €5 a whole pizza. It is by the fresh fish stall under a green awning.

eats.name: La Foca
eats.note: Pizza

eats.name: La Bitta
eats.note: This busy but friendly restaurant is in the more studenty area of Dorsoduro, and attracts a mixture of locals and tourists. They have some excellent Italian dishes, which are reflected in the prices,

eats.name: Osteria Ai Do Farai
eats.note: Serves fresh shell fish. Taste their spaghetti al dente with razor shells.

eats.name: Osteria Enoteca Ai Artisti
eats.note: An excellent restaurant, small but comfortable with a few tables alongside a tiny canal. Food is fresh and delicious, not too expensive. Large selection of wines. Menu changing daily.

eats.name: Chet Bar
eats.note: The closest thing to a dive bar you'll find in Venice, except that the cocktails actually are pretty good.

eats.name: Il Caffè Rosso
eats.note: Small but hugely popular café at Campo Santa Margherita. Serves coffee and sandwiches during the day, and excellent spritz during nights.

eats.name: Cantine del Vino gia Schiavi
eats.note: Inventive and delicious cicchetti; pile a plate with what you like, and the staff will pour you a glass of wine to match the selection. If it's too crowded inside, step out and find a space by the can

eats.name: Pizza 2000
eats.note: Pizza takeout

eats.name: Ostaria dai Zemei
eats.note: Down home cooking with Venezian style tapas

eats.name: Antico Forno
eats.note: A pizzeria

eats.name: Acqua e Mais
eats.note: Small plates

eats.name: Farini
eats.note: A bakery

eats.name: Ristorante Casa Cappellari
eats.note: Traditional Venetian cuisine with a warm atmosphere

eats.name: Antica Osteria Ruga Rialto
eats.note: Seafood specialties

eats.name: Cantina Do Mori
eats.note: Venetian tapas

eats.name: Cantina Do Spade
eats.note: Venetian cuisine

eats.name: Antico Dolo
eats.note: An old seafood restaurant close to Rialto bridge: food comes from the adjacent Rialto Market daily. A complete dinner excluding wines could cost €35 each more or less.

eats.name: Trattoria Antiche Carampane
eats.note: In the heart of Venice, steps away from the Rialto Bridge, is this renowned restaurant where distinguished Venetian cuisine is served in a familiar setting.

eats.name: Gelateria Il Doge
eats.note: Excellent ice cream, all made on the premises (a rarity in Venice). Plenty of vegan options.

eats.name: La Bottiglia
eats.note: A small wine bar with excellent reviews. They offer a small but constantly changing selection of wines, complemented by excellent Italian street food and snacks.

eats.name: Bacaro Quebrado
eats.note: Cosy tavern

eats.name: Arcicchetti Bakaro
eats.note: A bistro

eats.name: Il Refolo
eats.note: Nice restaurant at a small piazza. Very good pizza as well as a decent menu.

eats.name: Osteria Ae Cravate
eats.note: This little restaurant is frequented by the professors of the nearby university. Warm welcome and a good eat. Try their raw artichoke salad or their fish of the day.

eats.name: Osteria Mocenigo
eats.note: Little restaurant frequented by locals. Be sure to try their antipasti. Excellent desserts too.

eats.name: Pasticceria Rio Marin
eats.note: Coffee shop that serves excellent tiramisùs.

eats.name: Gelateria Alaska
eats.note: Ice cream made with natural ingredients by Carlo Pistacchi, not only the owner but an artist, a poet and a philosopher.

eats.name: Osteria da Filo
eats.note: An excellent place to fill up on some aperitifs and meet the local student crowd. Aperol Spritz is €2.50, a bargain for being in central Venice. The bar also hosts live music from time to time.

eats.name: Bacareto da Lele
eats.note: A Venetian institution that's been around since 1968. This minuscule bar serves cheap wine, a small glass is just one euro, and excellent cichetti to go along. Queuing is the norm, but the bartenders

eats.name: Bar Ducale
eats.note: A bistro

eats.name: We Love Italy fresh pasta to go - Rialto
Ristorante Al Conte Pescaor
eats.note: Cozy restaurant with a terrace serving fish dishes and sea food pasta

eats.name: Da Cherubino
eats.note: Italian dishes.

eats.name: Osteria Da Carla
eats.note: An Italian restaurant

eats.name: Antico Martini
eats.note: A luxury restaurant, favorite among the famous names of culture and business, the Antico Martini also attracts expert gourmets and famous personalities since the 1800s who come to enjoy unforgettable

eats.name: Restaurant La Caravella
eats.note: Historical place near St. Mark's Square, known since the 1960s, it has become a must if you like traditions. Offers some typical dishes and a large selection of wines. From May to September service is

eats.name: Caffe Quadri
eats.note: Opposite Caffè Florian, with similar prices.

eats.name: Bistrot de Venise
eats.note: Restaurant, cultural and enogastronomical meetings.

eats.name: Devils Forest Pub
eats.note: A traditional English style pub with a very fun atmosphere. It is located near the Rialto Bridge and tucked into a small alley near the Disney Store.

eats.name: Caffè Florian
eats.note: On the extravagant side there is Caffè Florian, on Piazza San Marco. It claims to be the oldest coffee house still in operation, established in 1720. The interior is about a century newer, and brings

eats.name: Harry's Bar-Ristorante
eats.note: The Bellini-cocktail was invented here. Ernest Hemingway was one of the most famous guests. Very pricy!

eats.name: Trattoria da Romano
eats.note: Famous people, including royalty, visited the place. The walls are covered with their photo's.

eats.name: La Perla Ai Bisatei
eats.note: Not an easy osteria to find but it is truly worth the detour for the kind service and cuisine.

eats.name: B - Alla Vecchia Pescheria
eats.note: Nice and simple restaurant, also with al fresco dining in the small square. Friendly staff. Try the local specialties.

eats.name: Trattoria Busa alla Torre Da Lele
eats.note: A typical trattoria, frequented by both tourists and locals. Excellent food.

eats.name: Osteriva
eats.note: Venetian cuisine with tasting menu. Mid-to-high priced.

eats.name: La Grande Cina
eats.note: Chinese cuisine

eats.name: Trattoria Andri
eats.note: Serves local Venetian seafood delicacies such as squid in ink over polenta (not as bad as it sounds), shrimp scampi and octopus, among other more common dishes. Water is served in Murano glass vases.

eats.name: La Cantinita
eats.note: Mexican cuisine

eats.name: Chiosco Chiringuito

next.name: Venice/Burano
next.note: Burano — Island famous for lace, textiles and colorfully painted houses.

next.name: Venice/Lido
next.note: Lido — The island of tranquility, a beach district 10 minutes by boat from San Marco, and where the Venice movie festival is held.

next.name: Mestre
next.note: Mestre — Town in the mainland, but still a part of Venice.

next.name: Venice/Murano
next.note: Murano — Nearby island famous for its glassware.

next.name: Venice/Torcello
next.note: Torcello — Nearby island with a 7th-century basilica church and an archeological museum.

next.name: Lake Garda
next.note: Lake Garda — An easy day trip by train, it is Italy's largest lake and stunning in scenery.

next.name: Eraclea
next.note: Eraclea — Typical for its pinewood and Laguna del Mort, 55 minutes from Venice by car or by boat.

next.name: Jesolo
next.note: Jesolo — Jesolo is one of the most important beaches in Italy, just 45 minutes from Venice by car or by boat (ferry from Treporti to Venice).

next.name: Padua
next.note: Padua (It. Padova) — 40 km west of Venice, home to the Basilica of St. Anthony, the Scrovegni Chapel, and the oldest Botanical Gardens in the world, among others.

next.name: Cortina d'Ampezzo
next.note: Cortina d'Ampezzo — Lovely alpine town, site of 1956 Winter Olympic Games. Great mountain scenery, might be very expensive. A couple of hours of car ride to the north of Venice, more than 3 hours by train and bus.
